links.outcome: Proportion of deliberately inserted AI contour errors corrected by clinician editing
links.effect: 72% of head and neck errors and 81% of prostate errors were removed in the editing step; most errors corrected by clinicians.
links.quote: Most errors, however, were corrected by clinicians, with 72% of the head and neck errors 81% of the prostate errors removed in the editing step.

links.outcome: Anchoring bias and detection/correction of incorrect AI outputs by clinicians
links.effect: Anchoring bias present when clinicians edit AI contours, more pronounced for some structures; most errors nonetheless corrected (72% head and neck, 81% prostate).
links.quote: Our safety and risk-mitigation exercise showed that anchoring bias is present when clinicians edit AI-generated contours, with the effect seemingly more pronounced for some structures over others.

links.effect: Time-saving was 36% (5.4 ± 2.1 minutes) for prostate and 67% (30.3 ± 8.7 minutes) for head and neck contouring.
links.quote: We found that OSAIRIS affords a significant time-saving of 36% (5.4 ± 2.1 minutes) when used for prostate contouring and 67% (30.3 ± 8.7 minutes) for head and neck contouring.

links.effect: Hausdorff distance best correlated with editing-time, outperforming dice, with Spearman 0.70 and Kendall 0.52.
links.quote: Combining editing time data with accuracy metrics, we found the Hausdorff distance best correlated with editing-time, outperforming dice, the industry-standard, with a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.70, and a Kendall coefficient of 0.52.

links.effect: Gold standard clinician contours were not rated more highly than AI-generated contours.
links.quote: Notably, our blinded clinician contour rating exercise showed that gold standard clinician contours are not rated more highly than the AI-generated contours.
